claims.statement: Desktop file-drop receivers register and participate only while enabled, and every native callback rechecks supportedPayload so retained hidden views and in-flight drags cannot bypass the enabled gate; ordinary pointer and scroll events pass through.
The desktop pane file receiver is the outermost overlay above Ghostty/Table content, accepts local files and private SFTP items only for SSH/SFTP panes, and is disabled during window layout dragging.
For a desktop target accepting SFTP items, a private remote payload wins before any file URL is requested, avoiding promised-file materialization; otherwise a file URL wins over bitmap data per item.

Mobile Workspace upload routing uses a window interaction bounded to the visible region, rejects hidden/detached or modally covered surfaces, tracks the active interaction, and deduplicates performDrop by session identity.

MobileTerminalDropTarget forwards uploadable providers to the Workspace delegate and other drops to Ghostty's original delegate; uninstall restores the original interaction and reattachment removes an earlier forwarder.

Mobile staged-upload classification accepts file URLs or eligible directory/data representations but excludes web URLs and unnamed text selections lacking an in-place file representation; requesting image attachments preserves image semantics.

Mobile upload staging copies provider files inside the file-representation callback using security-scoped coordinated reads, with separate per-item subdirectories; cancelled or empty loads discard staged results.

MobileWorkspaceView captures the upload destination before provider loading, cancels loading on disappearance/workspace/destination changes, and rejects cancelled or redirected results while allowing successful files and provider failures to be handled separately.
TFM and TFI Assistant file/image drop adapters import into the receiving conversation's composer and disable drops for archived conversations or pending approval/user-interaction cards.

Shared ConversationModel attachment imports count pending and loaded attachments against the 20-item limit, track asynchronous imports by pending ID, and ignore completions for removed/cancelled pending attachments.

The live attachment importer reads security-scoped regular files, rejects unsupported and legacy Office formats, limits inputs to 25 MiB and extracted text to 200000 characters, and limits normalized image output to 5 MiB.

SSH terminal uploads require a connected transfer configuration and nonempty resolved working directory observed from Ghostty's OSC 7 state; SFTP uses its browser directory, while Telnet has no upload destination.
Both platforms gate the SSH terminal upload convenience with terminalFileUpload Pro access, while SFTP browser uploads follow their own ungated entrypoint.

Desktop SSH upload preparation captures the destination and connection generation, prefers an independent SFTP connection, and can fall back to a PTY-owned SFTP channel on a current non-cancelled failure before preparing a local or remote batch.

Mobile upload preparation filters file URLs, requires transfer configuration and a destination, and guards asynchronous connection, home lookup and preflight with cancellation, preparation identity, connection generation and unchanged destination; SSH opens an independent SFTP client with a donated transfer context, while SFTP borrows the browser client/context, and enqueue or pending cancellation releases the donated owner without invalidating queued transfer references.

Local upload preparation enumerates files and empty directories, excludes resolved descendants outside the selected root, and preflights conflicts; remote directory mutation and coordinator enqueue occur in the later policy-driven enqueue phase.

Desktop SFTP drag sources publish own-process UUID-token payloads resolved through the transfer coordinator; SSH and SFTP receivers prepare remote copies with destination-specific directories and reject missing tokens or same-host self/descendant copies.

A desktop non-directory SFTP drag also exposes a public lazy file promise that downloads the dragged file into a unique temporary directory when requested, whereas directory rows publish only the private remote payload.

Desktop software Key drops populate editor buffers through SoftwareKeyFileImporter while editing is allowed; UTF-8 regular-file classification and name inference precede explicit Save's key inspection, certificate matching and persistence call.

TFM and TFI reuse DropTargetOverlay with caller-supplied title/detail/symbol/tone for hover feedback; the view disables hit testing and has no payload or transfer ownership, separate from post-drop WorkspaceUploadNotice.

When the desktop Key editor is in Security Key mode, a dropped file is read as a validated termind-fido2-v1 reference from a regular UTF-8 file at most 1 MiB, and explicit Save imports and validates that credential.
